P2C.comment: 1 goes to 3 and back, 2 goes to 4 and back
1 goes to 2, 2 to 3, and 3 back to 1

PDIM.comment: (-5,-2) and (5,2) become the new minimum and maximum of the plot range

PIX?.comment: A pixel given as an {x y} list in pixels

POS.comment: The first L is the 3rd character

POTENTIAL.comment: The field (X,Y) in the variables X and Y
The field (Y,X) in the variables X and Y

PREVAL.comment: A is the lower bound and B the upper

PROOT.comment: X^2 + 1 has the roots i and -i

PUTI.comment: Replaces element 1 and returns the next index, 2
After the last element the index wraps back to 1
After the last element the index wraps to 1 and flag 46 is set

PVARS.comment: Port 0 holds nothing; the number is its free memory

PX→C.comment: Pixel 0, 0 is the plot range's upper-left point
Pixel 65, 32 is the origin of the default plot window

QUAD.comment: s1 is +1 or -1, so the roots are 2 and 1
Flag -103 selects complex mode, so the roots i and -i are found

QUOTE.comment: A holds 5, yet the expression stays as it is

RAND.comment: Seed 123 gives the same number every time
The second call continues the sequence

RANM.comment: Seed 1 makes the values repeatable; 2 rows, 3 columns
Only the size of the given matrix is used

RCLALARM.comment: Alarm 1 comes back as date, time, text and repeat 0

RCLF.comment: Flags 1 and 3 set give 5 in the user flag word (1 + 4)
Masks the low three flags: 1 and 3 are set, 2 is clear

RDM.comment: A 2 by 2 matrix, filled row by row
A single size gives a vector; the fourth element is dropped

RECT.comment: After SPHERE, RECT clears flag -16 and leaves -15 set

RES.comment: A binary integer sets the resolution in pixels

RESULTANT.comment: Both have the root 1, so the result is 0

RKF.comment: y' = -y with y=1 at t=0, solved to t=1 within .00001

RKFERR.comment: One step of size .5 from t=0, y=1

RRK.comment: The partial derivatives of -Y, -1 and 0, extend the list

RSD.comment: Level 3 is B, level 2 is A, level 1 the trial solution Z
Z solves the system exactly, so the residual is zero

SAME.comment: Different names give 0, not a symbolic result

SCALE.comment: 2 units per 10 pixels in x, 1 in y

SEQ.comment: K runs from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.25

SHOW.comment: B is replaced by its contents, X stays as a name

SIGN.comment: The unit vector: (3,4) divided by its length, 5

SIMP2.comment: 12/18 reduces to 2/3: both numbers are divided by 6

SIZE.comment: Counts A, B, C and the two operators

SL.comment: The highest bit falls off the end, leaving 0

SREPL.comment: Both Bs are replaced; the count 2 is on level 1
Nothing found: the string is unchanged and the count is 0

START.comment: Runs the loop 5 times, doubling each time

STOALARM.comment: Date 1 January 2030, time 12:00, text Meet; the result is the alarm's index

STOF.comment: The binary integer 5 sets flags 1 and 3 and leaves 2 clear

STREAM.comment: Multiplies the elements one after another
Keeps the larger of each pair

STURMAB.comment: One root between 0 and 2; the polynomial is -2 at 0

STWS.comment: With 8 bits, 1FF is cut to FF

SYST2MAT.comment: The last column holds the constants moved to the left side: -3 and -1

S→H.comment: A is 41 and B is 42 in hexadecimal, each with its two digits in reverse order

TIME.comment: After setting 12:30 the clock has run a few seconds

TINC.comment: A rise of 15 K is a rise of 15 °C
A rise of 10 °C is 18 °F, so 68 becomes 86

TRANSIO.comment: The translation code, 2, is the last element of IOPAR

TRNC.comment: A negative count keeps 3 significant digits

TSTR.comment: 4 July 1991 at 18:45:12, shown on a 12-hour clock

TVARS.comment: Type 0 is real: only A is listed

TVMROOT.comment: Loan of 10000, 36 payments, 6% a year, 12 payments a year; solves PMT

UFACT.comment: Factors N out of the joule

UNPICK.comment: 99 replaces the object on level 2, the 2

UTPC.comment: 5 degrees of freedom, upper tail beyond 11.07

UTPN.comment: Mean 100, variance 225, so 115 is one standard deviation above the mean

UTPT.comment: At 0 the upper tail is half

V→.comment: In cylindrical mode a 2-element vector splits into radius and angle (not on the 48SX)

WHILE.comment: Doubles the value while it is below 100

XCOL.comment: Column 2 becomes the x column, so ΣX adds up that column

YCOL.comment: Column 1 becomes the y column, so ΣY adds up that column

XVOL.comment: Sets entries 1 and 2 of VPAR, the x bounds

YVOL.comment: Sets entries 3 and 4 of VPAR, the depth

ZVOL.comment: Sets entries 5 and 6 of VPAR, the height

^.comment: The square root of -8, so the result is complex

|.comment: X is replaced by 2 and Y by 3

Σ.comment: The sum of N^2 for N from 1 to 10

Σ+.comment: Two single values make a one-column matrix
Adds a fourth data row, so NΣ gives 4

↑MATCH.comment: Rewritten by distributing; the 1 reports a match

↓MATCH.comment: Rewritten by distributing; the 1 reports a match

→.comment: Binds 3 to a and 4 to b

→ARRY.comment: A 2 by 2 matrix: the list gives rows and columns

∞.comment: The limit of 1/X as X goes to infinity

∫.comment: 0 to 1 to within .00001; the second value is the error estimate

RR.comment: The lowest bit wraps to the top
In an 8-bit word the lowest bit wraps to 128

RL.comment: The top bit wraps to the bottom

RLB.comment: The top byte wraps to the bottom

RRB.comment: In a 16-bit word the two bytes swap
